title: GTA 6 HUD Settings: Make Your Screen Easier to Read
description: Make GTA 6 easier to read from your couch or monitor. See where Rockstar puts HUD scaling, subtitles, navigation, and notifications, then use a one-minute drive to test what works for you. Independent commentary with synthetic narration.
footage_credit: Rockstar Games, GTA VI Launch Trailer and Out Now. https://www.rockstargames.com/VI/media/videos
sources: Rockstar Support — GTA 6 settings menu and UI categories

chapters.title: Make the screen easier to read
lines: You can make Grand Theft Auto Six easier to read without turning the screen into a wall of prompts.
Start with the information you miss most. Maybe a subtitle disappears before you finish reading it, or the notifications pull your eye away from the road.
We'll go through readability, subtitles, and notifications, then I'll show you a quick way to decide what to keep.
Start from the pause menu, select Settings, and look for U I. That's where Rockstar groups the on-screen options in this guide.

chapters.title: Start with scaling and readability
lines: If you keep leaning toward the screen in Grand Theft Auto Six, look for Scaling and Readability under U I in Settings.
Start from the seat you actually play in. Something that looks fine close to a monitor can feel tiny across a living room.
Change one option, return to the game, and check whether you can read a prompt at a glance.
Use the smallest change that solves the problem. If you can read comfortably without your attention leaving the road or the scene, you've found a good place to stop.
chapters.short_title: GTA 6 HUD Text Too Small? Start Here
chapters.short_description: Check Scaling and Readability in GTA 6, then test the change from the seat where you actually play.

chapters.title: Make subtitles work in motion
lines: For subtitles in Grand Theft Auto Six, open Settings and look under U I for Subtitles and Captions.
I would test these during dialogue while the camera is moving. A quiet menu won't tell you how well you'll catch a line while watching the scene.
See if you can follow the dialogue without losing track of what's happening around the character.
Then try the same idea in a brighter area. A comfortable setting is one you can use across scenes, even when the background changes.
chapters.short_title: GTA 6 Subtitles: Try This While Driving
chapters.short_description: Find Subtitles and Captions in GTA 6 and test your setup during dialogue while the camera moves.

chapters.title: Keep directions you actually use
lines: Rockstar lists Navigation as its own group under U I. That makes it a separate decision from how large the on-screen text should be.
I would test it on a short route with a couple of turns. Pay attention to the moment you decide where to turn.
If you hesitate or look away from the road, keep more guidance while you learn the route.
Once you're comfortable, adjust a single option and run the same stretch again. The comparison tells you whether the change helps you drive.

chapters.title: Reduce distractions in the HUD
lines: If too much keeps pulling your eye away in Grand Theft Auto Six, look for HUD Notifications and Progress Notifications under U I.
Think about those groups separately. You may want an on-screen status update while driving, but prefer to check progress in a quiet moment.
Change one option, take a short drive, and see if you still catch the updates you care about.
Remember which setting you changed. If you start missing information you relied on, put that setting back and try a different one.
chapters.short_title: GTA 6 HUD Notifications: Keep What Matters
chapters.short_description: Tune HUD Notifications and Progress Notifications separately, then test the changes on a short route.

chapters.title: Take one short test drive
lines: Here's the quick test I would use. Pick a route you know, play at your usual distance, and give yourself a minute.
Can you read a prompt? Can you follow dialogue while moving? Can you catch the notifications that matter without hunting for them?
Change the option linked to the first thing you missed, then repeat the route.
Keep what helps in motion. If you want to start over, Rockstar lists Restore All and Restore Default at the bottom of the settings screen.
